The site is Canopy Guardian — Urban Street Tree Health & Watering Monitor, a dashboard web application for Urban forestry street tree health reporting.

Owner brief: "Our neighbourhood urban forestry committee monitors newly planted street trees and needs a community health dashboard. Residents should be able to view a map-aligned table of street trees, check species and watering frequency, and log a watering event or report insect damage. Logged maintenance actions must be saved on the server and immediately update the tree health dashboard."

Locale & copy conventions (en-US): Use $ prices, US English spelling and month-day dates. Today's date is 11 October 2026; date all entries, bookings, deadlines, and activity in the weeks after 11 October 2026.

Visual identity & layout lock: Match the exact brand header, logo treatment, navigation bar, typography, card geometry, and light colour palette of the attached reference image (docs/design/training/tr-22/reference.jpg).

Art direction: Canopy Guardian — Urban Street Tree Health & Watering Monitor: the page for urban forestry street tree health reporting, in a light palette, recognisable by its own token prefix rather than by a shared template.

Use this exact Light Mode colour palette: #047857 (cg-green), #84cc16 (cg-lime), #0f172a (cg-slate), #1e293b (cg-card), #334155 (cg-border), #f8fafc (cg-text), #94a3b8 (cg-muted). The primary accent colour carries the single primary action.

Structural constants: control-radius 8px, content-frame 1200px, control-border 1px solid var(--cg-border), page-padding 1.5rem. Keep every form control clearly identifiable in its unfocused state with a distinct background fill or icon cue.

Strictly avoid: a chart decorative enough to hide the number it reports; a second accent colour competing with the primary action; placeholder text standing in for a visible label; a modal or step wizard hiding part of the form; colour alone carrying an error with no message naming the field.

STEP 1 OF 4 (LIGHT MODE) — INITIAL OVERVIEW & READY WORKSPACE:

Render the initial landing state of Canopy Guardian — Urban Street Tree Health & Watering Monitor as a visitor first meets it on the primary workspace. Top-to-bottom structure: a brand header, then a navigation bar, then a main content area, then a content section, then the working form, then a footer.

Show the active overview/dashboard/ledger/catalogue surface populated with realistic, internally consistent records and totals, alongside the ready-to-use interactive form with visible labels for every control ("Tree identifier", "Steward name", "Maintenance timestamp", "Maintenance action", "Water volume (litres)", "Observation notes").

User journey context: Search street trees by neighbourhood block and check recent watering dates. Open a specific tree profile to view species, planting year, and drought risk rating. Submit a tree watering confirmation, view the updated status, and reload the summary page.

Include editorial photography where appropriate to the subject, a concise social-proof or status summary row, and the complete site footer.
